page.overview:
What is Durthang?

Durthang was an old castle located in the mountains of northern Mordor, and one of the many Orc-holds along the northern mountains there. It stood "high up in the" northern Ephel Dúath above the valley of Udûn "a few miles north" of Carach Angren where a mountain spur branched away south-east to the Isenmouthe. A stony road with "no wall or parapet along the edge" ran "winding down from" Durthang and turned east "along a shelf cut in the" southern side of the mountain spur, down into the Plateau of Gorgoroth and beside the spur to the Isenmouthe.

Either before or after Durthang was built, some unspecified "road-builders of old" made the road that led from Durthang to the Isenmouthe in Mordor. Durthang may possibly have been "originally a fortress of Gondor" because, in the aftermath of Sauron's defeat in the War of the Last Alliance at the end of the Second Age in the year 3441, the Gondorians had constructed several fortresses overlooking the entrance to Mordor like the Towers of the Teeth or the Tower of Cirith Ungol. At first "the centre of the Watch" was Minas Ithil and the fortresses and castles that watched over Mordor were fully maintained and manned. However, as Gondor's power began to decline, they began to be neglected from the reign of King Atanatar II.

After the Great Plague devastated Gondor in the year 1636, "the Watch" It is possible that this included Durthang. by the Wainriders, the Morannon and the Towers of the Teeth were still maintained. In the year 1980 when the Witch-king came to Mordor and gathered the Nazgûl there, Durthang was repaired as an Orc-hold and fully garrisoned by Sauron's forces.

On Sunday, March 18 of the year 3019, Frodo Baggins and Samwise Gamgee caught a glimpse of Durthang when they came to the road that led away from "that orc-tower" to the Isenmouthe. until that evening, Frodo and Samwise began to head down the road, which they found was not very broad. passed them by. "before dawn" on March 19, some of the Host of the West ventured "into Mordor and destroyed the fortresses in the north of the land". It is possible that Durthang was one of these fortresses, but its exact fate remains untold.
